## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished presentation. To learn more about Quarto presentations see <https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/>.

## Bullets

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes:

- Content authored with markdown
- Output from executable code

## Code

When you click the **Render** button a presentation will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r data}
# first, import all necessary packages
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr) # seems very useful, ill use it just for conditional removal of rows from our data

# get our data set
df <- `2026.08.MD`

# take the dataset relevant to us
ds <- df[c("V1","V7","V105","V77")] 

# rename columns to be more expressive
colnames(ds) <- c("Date","IndustrialProduction","ConsumerPriceIndex","FedFundRate") 

# remove the weird two rows from the original data
ds <- ds[-c(1:2), ] 

# check types of the columns, they are all charater type
print("Check the types of the columns to see if we must adjust them")
sapply(ds, class) 

# they were all character type, convert to the correct respective types
#as.numeric(ds$`Industrial Production`)
#as.numeric(ds$`Consumer Price Index`)
#as.numeric(ds$`Fed Fund Rate`)
#as.Date(ds$Date, format="%d/%m/%Y")

ds <- transform(
  ds, `Date` = as.Date(ds$Date, format="%d/%m/%Y"), `IndustrialProduction` = as.numeric(ds$`IndustrialProduction`), `ConsumerPriceIndex` = as.numeric(ds$`ConsumerPriceIndex`), `FedFundRate` = as.numeric(ds$`FedFundRate`))

# check they are the correct type
print("Check the types of the columns again to ensure they are correct")
sapply(ds, class) 
ds
# we now have the correct types

# now we will remove data from the end of 2019 onwards to avoid looking at the anomalous data from covid-19. we use dplyr
ds <- ds %>%
  filter(`Date`<"2020-01-01")

ds
```

Now that we have cleaned and prepared our data, we can move onto to exploring it.

```{r visual}
# get an initial look into them by plotting them
ggplot(aes(x = `Date`, y = `IndustrialProduction`), data = ds) + geom_point()
ggplot(aes(x = `Date`, y = `ConsumerPriceIndex`), data = ds) + geom_point()
ggplot(aes(x = `Date`, y = `FedFundRate`), data = ds) + geom_point()
```
